canonical_statement: For every abstract simplicial complex on a linearly ordered vertex type, the unreduced integral chain groups freely generated by its (n+1)-vertex faces admit the alternating vertex-deletion boundary, and two consecutive boundaries compose to zero.
domain_and_universes: universe u; V : Type u; LinearOrder V; K : AbstractSimplicialComplex V; integral Finsupp chain groups; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: the vertex type carries the selected linear order
K is an AbstractSimplicialComplex (so all singletons occur and every nonempty subset of a face is a face)
conclusion: There exists a family of additive boundary maps on integral finite-support chains, agreeing on every basis simplex with the alternating sum of ordered codimension-one faces, whose consecutive maps compose to zero.
coefficient_and_orientation_policy: Unreduced integral finite chains. An n-simplex is a face of cardinality n+1. The increasing enumeration from LinearOrder V fixes orientation, and face i deletes its ith vertex. There is no degree -1 group or empty simplex.
functoriality_policy: The intake's induced-map component is deferred: arbitrary vertex maps need an orientation sign and may identify vertices. This statement node freezes the construction and boundary-square root without silently assuming that unresolved bridge.

killed: changed integral coefficients to rational coefficients
moved the vertex-type binder from universal to existential scope
changed the degree-zero boundary convention to require d_0 = 0

degenerate_cases: Empty vertex types are permitted (the unique empty complex has no nonempty faces). Degree zero chains are included, while the root only asserts d_n after degree n+1 and d_n d_(n+1)=0; no augmentation or reduced degree -1 boundary is introduced. Infinite vertex sets and infinitely many simplices are allowed, but each chain has finite support.
status_boundary: This freezes and elaborates the exact ordered unreduced integral boundary-square target. It neither proves the target nor supplies source, anchor, obligation-tree, validation, release, or theorem-completion evidence.
